core_obligations: (1) implies sheaf: for a covering $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i=1,\ldots,n}$ of $X_{affine, \etale}$ the sheaf condition reduces to exactness of the tensor-amplified $\check{\mathrm{C}}$ech sequence, which holds because $\mathcal{O}_X(U) \to \prod \mathcal{O}_X(U_i)$ is faithfully flat (standard-covering $\check{\mathrm{C}}$ech lemma) and ff-exactness applies (proof lines 539-551).

(1) implies quasi-coherent: transport a free presentation of $\mathcal{F}(U)$ over $R = \mathcal{O}_X(U)$ along the tensor isomorphisms (right exactness of tensor) to get presentations over every $U' \to U$, i.e., a presentation of the restriction to the localized site (proof lines 551-570).
(2) implies (3): quasi-coherence is intrinsic (cited Modules on Sites lemma), so the site equivalence restricts to quasi-coherent modules (proof lines 572-578).

(3) implies (1): for $\mathcal{F}$ corresponding to $\mathcal{G}$ on $X$ and $h : U \to U'$ in $X_{affine, \etale}$, compute $\mathcal{F}(U) = \Gamma(U, h^*(f')^*\mathcal{G})$ and conclude by the affine tensor lemma for pullbacks (proof lines 580-607).
proof_roadmap: Prove sheafness from faithful flatness of the standard \'etale $\check{\mathrm{C}}$ech algebra.
Prove quasi-coherence by transporting free presentations.
Transport along the site equivalence by intrinsicness.
Compute sections of pullbacks for the converse.
difficulty_reason: The proof is a three-way equivalence with real module arguments: (1) implies sheafness via faithful flatness of the $\check{\mathrm{C}}$ech algebra of a standard \'etale covering and the ff-exactness lemma, then implies quasi-coherence by transporting free presentations along the tensor isomorphisms; (2) implies (3) by intrinsicness of quasi-coherence under the site equivalence; (3) implies (1) by computing sections of pullbacks and applying the affine-tensor lemma.
